>
> Error in data.frame(r1 = r1, r2 = r2, r3 = r3, r4 = r4, r5 = r5) :
>   arguments imply differing number of rows: 860, 3600 In addition: Warning message:
> In r1 + r2 + r3 + r4 :
>   longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

This occurs even when I am starting from scratch (i.e., including completing part 1 again). I wonder if anyone has encountered this problem before?

Many thanks,
Taren

messages.body_plain:
Dear Hervé,

Thanks, I was not aware of a way to merge the binary files, but if you know a way how to do it then that may work. GGIR should be able to handle long measurements, but i have experience testing this for files with more than 30 days of data.

A more simple solution would be to process the files separately and then concatenate the report files afterwards, which will have the obvious disadvantage that the transition days may be partially missed or overlap.

To address the latter you could instead first process the binary files with part1 of the GGIR code followed by concatenating the resulting RData milestone files, while paying attention to correct continuation of the timestamps.

Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
I found a way to merge the .bin files.

Here is the R code :

mydata1=read.csv(file="export1.bin", header=FALSE,blank.lines.skip=FALSE)

mydata2=read.csv(file="export2.bin", header=FALSE, skip=59,blank.lines.skip=FALSE)

mydata=rbind(mydata1,mydata2)

write.table(mydata, "merge.bin", quote=FALSE, col.names = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

Finally, you have to replace manually the string

"Number of Pages:61218" in the merge.bin file to be the sum of those in export1.bin and export2.bin. My skills in R are not developped enough to to that automatically....

Looks like everything goes well using this file with g.shell.GGIR.
The two merged files had 10 minutes of no recording, i changed the frequency from 10 to 50 Hz between the two.

messages.subject: GGIR publications
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am trying to compile a list of scientific publications which have used the GGIR package. Being able to demonstrate the impact of GGIR on science may help us to get funding for future enhancements.

Can I please ask you to review the publication list below and let me know if I have missed a publication that used GGIR? In particular the non-methodological publication-list is hard for me to update as this is not the type of literature I normally read. Also, the further away scientists are from the methodological work the less they seem to care about correctly citing the underlying methodological work. For example, Horta et al in 2015 used the package but did not cite any of the underlying methodological papers, which makes it hard for me to learn about the existence of such a paper.

Cheers, Vincent

Non-methodological scientific publications using GGIR:

Afshar et al. Changes in physical activity after bariatric surgery: using objective and self-reported measures. Surg Obes Relat Dis. 2016 Sep 13. pii: S1550-7289(16)30698-0. doi: 10.1016/j.soard.2016.09.012.

Bell, J. A. et al. Healthy obesity and objective physical activity. Am. J. Clin. Nutr. (2015). doi:10.3945/ajcn.115.110924

Esteban-Cornejo, I. et al. Physical Activity throughout Adolescence and Cognitive Performance at 18 Years of Age. Med. Sci. Sports Exerc. 47, 2552–7 (2015).

Hiden et al Prediction of workflow execution time using provenance traces: practical applications in medical data processing. IEEE eScience Conference, Baltimore 2016

Horta, B. L. et al. Objectively measured physical activity and sedentary-time are associated with arterial stiffness in Brazilian young adults. Atherosclerosis 243, 148–54 (2015).

Sabia, S. et al. Physical Activity and Adiposity Markers at Older Ages: Accelerometer Vs Questionnaire Data. J. Am. Med. Dir. Assoc. 16, 438.e7–438.e13 (2015).

da Silva, I. C. et al. Physical activity levels in three Brazilian birth cohorts as assessed with raw triaxial wrist accelerometry. Int. J. Epidemiol. (2014).

Hi Inacio,
For experiments that last only a couple of hours you should adjust argument windowsizes to be meaningful relative to the duration of your experiment. For example, windowsizes = c(5, 300, 300), would require at least 5 minutes of data (300 seconds) as it attempts to do non-wear detection per 5 minute window.
Cheers, Vincent
